description: We are a team of engineers passionate about data analytics, prototyping, and geospatial solutions applied to land and agricultural management. We are dedicated to transforming satellite data into practical tools for early warning and climate mitigation. Our project has a direct impact on farmers, emergency response teams, and environmental managers.
summary: We developed GeoFire / KILLARI, a community-driven web and mobile platform for wildfire risk monitoring, early warning, and 5-day predictive forecasting in Peru. For many farming families in northern Cusco, a single wildfire can wipe out crops, livestock, and years of livelihood—in September 2025 alone, COEN–INDECI reported 100 hectares of natural cover destroyed in Echarate (La Convención). GeoFire bridges the gap between complex orbital data and rural communities across Echarate, Maranura, Santa Teresa, and Vilcabamba. Our core scientific contribution lies in harmonizing 26 years of historical thermal data (2000–2026) from NASA's MODIS and VIIRS sensors—reconciling their spatial and radiometric differences—to improve 5-day wildfire prediction across a 294-cell H3 hexagonal grid (showing preliminary hit rates between 33.3% and 66.7%). Combined with NASA GIBS imagery, privacy-first citizen reporting, and KILLARI (a RAG-powered AI assistant), GeoFire empowers farmers and local authorities to understand their territory, anticipate danger, and make evidence-based prevention decisions.
details:
What exactly does it do?

GeoFire / KILLARI is a scientifically grounded decision-support system for wildfire prevention and community surveillance. Specifically:

  • Harmonizes multi-decadal thermal anomaly records (2000–2026) from NASA's MODIS and VIIRS sensors, correcting cross-sensor discrepancies to improve predictive modeling and historical trend analysis.
  • Predicts 5-day wildfire risk levels, operational hotspots, and watchlists across 294 resolution-6 H3 hexagonal cells in La Convención (Cusco), achieving a preliminary hit rate of 33.3% to 66.7% in evaluated historical cases.
  • Visualizes real-time NASA FIRMS detections, NASA GIBS satellite imagery, inter-annual fire histories, and custom polygon analytics through a responsive Material Design 3 Dark interface (web and Android via Capacitor).
  • Empowers rural farmers and citizens to log offline-first, geo-referenced smoke and fire sightings with photos (via IndexedDB and privacy-safe Supabase sharing) to validate orbital detections on the ground.
  • Educates & Assists users through KILLARI, a local BM25 + DeepSeek conversational AI assistant that cites official project documents, paired with an on-the-ground training program designed for local agricultural communities.

How does it work?

The project combines a rigorous scientific and technical workflow with community field validation:

  1. Multi-Sensor Harmonization & Data Ingestion (2000–2026): We ingest 26 years of historical fire detections from NASA FIRMS (MODIS and VIIRS), satellite imagery from NASA GIBS, meteorological variables from Open-Meteo, and topography (elevation, slope, aspect) from Copernicus DEM, filtered specifically to Echarate, Maranura, Santa Teresa, and Vilcabamba.
  2. Scientific Ablation & H3 Predictive Modeling: Our Python ML pipeline (scikit-learn, pandas, pyarrow) models risk across 294 resolution-6 H3 hexagonal cells. To rigorously prove our scientific contribution, we evaluate the exact same predictive architecture with and without MODIS–VIIRS harmonization against official fire records on strictly out-of-sample future dates, measuring lead time, hit rate, and false-alarm reduction. Daily pre-computed artifacts are served via FastAPI on Fly.io.
  3. Accessible Map Visualization & Citizen Reporting: Through a Cloudflare Pages frontend, users explore 5-day alert levels (rather than confusing raw probabilities). When farmers spot smoke or fire, they mark the map; reports are saved locally in IndexedDB (with JSON backup/restore) and shared anonymously to trigger nearby alerts via Supabase Edge Functions and Resend.
  4. AI-Guided Interpretation (KILLARI): Farmers and local actors can ask questions in plain language. The browser retrieves verified context using a local BM25 index and routes it through a secure Supabase llm-proxy to DeepSeek, returning clear answers with cited sources.
  5. Community Training & Quasi-Experimental Impact Evaluation: Technology is paired with human capacity building—starting with a 90-day field pilot training 30 farmers across 2 communities, measuring knowledge acquisition via pre- and post-training evaluations, and comparing fire incidence against control communities.

What benefits does it have?

  • Environmental: Protects high-risk Andean-Amazonian transition ecosystems in La Convención (where single events like the September 2025 Echarate fire destroyed 100 hectares of natural cover). We are testing a planning hypothesis of a 10% reduction in wildfire incidence across intervened territories compared to control communities under equivalent climatic baselines.
  • Social: Democratizes satellite science for rural farmers. Our goal is that at least 80% of trained participants (96 out of 120 farmers) accurately interpret satellite risk layers and submit actionable ground reports, protecting their families, livestock, and community infrastructure.
  • Economic: Prevents devastating agricultural and livestock losses for smallholder farmers while reducing emergency suppression costs for local governments. By using pre-computed daily ML artifacts, local-first storage, and serverless functions, the platform remains financially sustainable for regional municipalities and agricultural cooperatives.
